title: Inference — Skill Check
description: Build the smallest supported inference from multiple clues and identify the evidence that earns it.
subject: rla
author: Chee Skool
reviewNotes: Unseen independent check; no hints, retries, or guided scaffolding.

questions.prompt: What can the reader reasonably infer from Mr. Vale’s actions after reading the message?

options.text: He has decided to cancel the workshop.
options.whyWrong: He prepares the space for a new activity rather than ending work.

options.text: He expects the borrowed stage lights to arrive soon.
He wants Mara to repaint the loading door.
options.whyWrong: No evidence connects the door to painting.

options.text: He learned that the neighboring theater lost the lights.
options.whyWrong: His smile and preparations point toward arrival, not loss.

explanation.whyCorrect: This choice best matches the passage: He expects the borrowed stage lights to arrive soon.
explanation.quickTip: Keep the answer within the passage’s actual scope.

questions.prompt: Which detail most strongly supports the inference that the morning plan is about to change?

options.text: Mara expected to paint scenery.
options.whyWrong: This gives her original expectation but not evidence of the change by itself.

options.text: Mr. Vale held a roll of blue tape.
options.whyWrong: The tape becomes meaningful with later actions, but alone is weak.

options.text: The workshop has a storage cabinet.
options.whyWrong: This detail does not show a schedule change.

options.text: Mr. Vale leaves the paint cans unopened and tells students to leave their brushes on the table.

explanation.whyCorrect: This choice best matches the passage: Mr. Vale leaves the paint cans unopened and tells students to leave their brushes on the table.
explanation.quickTip: Keep the answer within the passage’s actual scope.

questions.prompt: Why does Mara begin moving the last cart before Mr. Vale asks her?

options.text: She has inferred from the preparations and arriving van what needs to happen next.
She wants to leave the workshop early.
options.whyWrong: No clue suggests she plans to leave.

options.text: She dislikes painting scenery.
options.whyWrong: The passage never states or implies this.

options.text: She knows the black cases contain paint.
options.whyWrong: The context points to stage lights, not paint.

explanation.whyCorrect: This choice best matches the passage: She has inferred from the preparations and arriving van what needs to happen next.
explanation.quickTip: Keep the answer within the passage’s actual scope.

questions.prompt: Which pair of clues most strongly supports the inference that the black cases contain the borrowed lights?

options.text: Mr. Vale checks his watch, and Mara carries a brush.
options.whyWrong: These details do not identify the cases.

options.text: The workshop has a loading door, and the van is in the service lane.
options.whyWrong: These show delivery context but not what is being delivered.

options.text: Mr. Vale has been waiting for six portable lights, then marks six stage positions just before the van arrives.
The cases are black, and the paint cans are unopened.
options.whyWrong: Color of the cases does not identify their contents.

explanation.whyCorrect: This choice best matches the passage: Mr. Vale has been waiting for six portable lights, then marks six stage positions just before the van arrives.
explanation.quickTip: Keep the answer within the passage’s actual scope.

questions.prompt: Which inference goes beyond what the clues earn?

options.text: The first hour may be used to test or place the lights.
options.whyWrong: The six marks, cords, and schedule change support this.

options.text: Mr. Vale likely received a delivery update on his phone.
options.whyWrong: His reaction and immediate preparations support this.

options.text: Mara understands enough of the situation to anticipate the next task.
Mr. Vale plans to replace the school’s entire lighting system permanently.

explanation.whyCorrect: This choice best matches the passage: Mr. Vale plans to replace the school’s entire lighting system permanently.
explanation.quickTip: Keep the answer within the passage’s actual scope.

questions.prompt: Which evidence best supports the inference that Mr. Vale is preparing for equipment setup rather than simply receiving a delivery?

options.text: A van turns into the service lane.
options.whyWrong: That supports delivery but not setup.

options.text: He marks six stage positions and asks for extension cords before the van arrives.
He smiles at a phone message.
options.whyWrong: This suggests good news but not specifically setup.

options.text: Mara had expected to paint.
options.whyWrong: This only establishes the original plan.

explanation.whyCorrect: This choice best matches the passage: He marks six stage positions and asks for extension cords before the van arrives.
explanation.quickTip: Keep the answer within the passage’s actual scope.

curriculum.learningObjective: Build the smallest supported inference from multiple clues and identify the evidence that earns it.
